subject: SPAN
title: Civils&Cultrs Of Latin Amer
description:
Explores the history of the Spanish-speaking regions of Latin America, from
pre-Colombian civilizations, to the Spanish conquest, to the present. Students will broaden their
knowledge of major geographical, political, religious and literary aspects of Latin American culture.
enrollment_requirements: Prerequisites: SPAN 201 and SPAN 202; or SPAN 211 and SPAN 212; or Consent of Instructor

subject: SPAN
title: Specialized Translation Work I
description:
Hands-on translation from English to Spanish and vice versa with a focus on specialized
texts (e.g., scientific, technical, legal, financial, etc.). Through a blend of practical exercises,
real-world translation projects, and peer collaboration, participants will develop and refine their
translation skills in a supportive and interactive environment. May be taken before or after
SETI/SPAN 423.
enrollment_requirements: SPAN 420 and SETI 420 Prerequisites: SPAN 330 or consent of instructor

subject: SPAN
title: Healthcare Term Interpreters
description:
Focuses on development of students' knowledge of medical terminology both in English
and Spanish. Topics include terminology associated with physiology, common disorders, diagnostic
tests, and treatments related to different body systems. May be taken before or after SETI/SPAN
451.
enrollment_requirements: SPAN 452 and SETI 452 Prerequisite: SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 or Consent of Instructor

subject: SPAN
title: Masterpieces Of Latin Amer Lit
description:
Advanced literature course that explores major Latin American Literary works.
Enhances students' knowledge of Latin American literature, history and culture. Develops critical
thinking and improves students' reading and writing skills and Spanish language vocabulary.
enrollment_requirements: SPAN 461 Prerequisite: SPAN 301 or SPAN 302 and SPAN 310

subject: SPAN
title: Capstone In Spanish
description:
Seminar-style course on a specialized topic related to Hispanic literature, culture,
linguistics, or translation. As the culminating experience of the course, students complete a
substantial academic project related to the topic. Students also engage in career development
activities including résumé preparation and mock interviews.
enrollment_requirements: Pre-requisite: Senior standing as a Spanish major or Consent of instructor

subject: SPED
title: Ind With Disabilities
description:
Explores disability studies and special education through an interdisciplinary lens by
integrating multiple methods. Investigates major types of disabilities and giftedness, including
definitions, causes, characteristics, and educational implications. Topics include disability
perspectives and social, legal, and educational considerations of disability issues. Substantial focus
on writing. Students must earn a C- or better to fulfill the Graduation Writing Assessment
Requirement (GWAR).
enrollment_requirements: UDGE - Requisite: Successful completion of Golden Four GE Areas (1A, 1B, 1C, 2)

subject: SPED
title: Typical Atypical Development
description:
Focus on typical and atypical development from the prenatal stage to adulthood and the
implications for learning. Emphasis on atypical development associated with various disabilities and
risk conditions. Resilience and protective factors and their impact on learning. Theories of typical
and atypical child development, including educational and home settings, schools, communities, and
culture are integrated. Changed from SPED 530 effective F17.
enrollment_requirements: Junior Standing or enrolled in Post-baccalaureate Pre-Credential program

subject: THTR
title: Acting I: Foundations
description:
Exercises and activities that emphasize voice, movement, concentration, and relaxation
practices foundational to the craft of acting. Includes improvisation, monologues, and multi-character
scenes. Introduces histories and theories of select acting practices.

subject: THTR
title: Vocal Empowerment on Stage Scr
description:
Students will learn to use their presence and voice both on-screen and in-person.
Through studying and creating presentations and performances for the stage as well as digital and
social media, students will learn to use their voices for social change, and the empowerment of
themselves and their communities. Introduces the fundamentals of on-camera work and vocal
techniques for effective and expressive performance.

subject: THTR
title: Acting II: Characterization
description:
Overview of the history, theory, and practice of select intermediate acting and applied
theatre practices. Character work, scene study, ensemble building, and improvisation are developed
through in-class exercises and service-learning activities in the community.

subject: THTR
title: Topics in Thtr & Performance S
description:
Explores diverse works, methods, and theories of performance and theatre centering on
communities with shared histories of marginalization across the globe. Approaches theatre and
performance forms through critical lenses relevant to the topic, such as ethnicity, race, gender,
sexuality, colonialism, resistance, and liberation. Topics vary by semester.
enrollment_requirements: UDGE - Requisite: Successful completion of Golden Four GE Areas (1A, 1B, 1C, 2)
class_notes:
Explore the stories and histories of a diverse range of LGBTQ+ people in theatre and performance,
on stage, on screen, and beyond. Learn about the theories that inform, and are inspired by, queer
artists' performance practices. Reflect on queer triumph and tragedy, queer joy and genius, and the
cultural significance to the world of LGBTQ+ performance

subject: THTR
title: Topics in Thtr & Performance S
description:
Explores diverse works, methods, and theories of performance and theatre centering on
communities with shared histories of marginalization across the globe. Approaches theatre and
performance forms through critical lenses relevant to the topic, such as ethnicity, race, gender,
sexuality, colonialism, resistance, and liberation. Topics vary by semester.
enrollment_requirements: UDGE - Requisite: Successful completion of Golden Four GE Areas (1A, 1B, 1C, 2)
class_notes:
Explore the stories and histories of activist theatre for social change; performance-based strategies
employed by diverse communities. Learn about how performing artists taken on social issues and
engaged in activism by devising performance-based interventions on stage, on screen, and via
multimedia. Be inspired by impactful stories overcoming adversity and by performances that give a
voice to historically underrepresented communities.

subject: THTR
title: Global Thtr & Perfom Hist II
description:
Examines theatre and performance in relation to historical, social, and political
influences in the Americas, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, Asia, South Asia, and Oceania, primarily
beginning in the 18th century. Explores plays, images, or historical accounts of formal productions
and performances, as well as other types of performance, storytelling, or representation, such as
protests, ceremonies, or political debates.
enrollment_requirements: UDGE - Requisite: Successful completion of Golden Four GE Areas (1A, 1B, 1C, 2)

subject: THTR
title: Teaching Drama To Children
description:
Students will participate in theater games, improvisations, and other tasks that will
prepare them to design and implement dramatic activities as a learning tool. Theater in a broader
context will also be examined.
enrollment_requirements: UDGE - Requisite: Successful completion of Golden Four GE Areas (1A, 1B, 1C, 2)
class_notes: Cross-listed course

subject: THTR
title: Perf Presence on Stage Screen
description:
Introduces effective practices and performance techniques specific to cultivating
students personal brands and vocal identities, both on screen and on the stage. Students explore
artist development, professional networking techniques, the generation of original material, and
advanced audience engagement strategies related to in-person performance as well digital and
social media.

subject: THTR
title: Acting IV: Prep for Profession
description:
Develops professionalization skills like grant writing, resume building, auditioning,
preparing self-submissions, creating a reel, and polishing an online presence. Covers performance
skills and knowledge inherent to various career options on stage, on screen, and beyond--from
acting and directing to casting, producing, arts management, and teaching. Includes practice-based
scenarios for various contexts.
enrollment_requirements: THTR 480: Junior Standing
class_notes: Prerequisite course required. Consult CSUCI Catalog

subject: THTR
title: Capstone: Community Collaborat
description:
Students will blend their knowledge and practice to develop and execute a
service-learning theatre or performance project in collaboration with a community partner.
enrollment_requirements: THTR 499: Senior Standing
class_notes: Prerequisite course required. Consult CSUCI Catalog

subject: UNIV
title: Univ Life & College Success
description:
Introduces first-year students to university life, the structure and policies of the
University and development of strategies and skills to help insure success in college. Students will
be expected to apply learning skills to other courses during the semester.

subject: UNIV
title: Critical Think & Univ Mission
description:
This course develops advanced critical thinking and analytical skills through
engagement with the university's mission pillars of multiculturalism, internationalism,
interdisciplinarity, and community engagement. Students learn to evaluate arguments, analyze
complex issues, and apply logical reasoning across diverse contexts. Through structured discussion,
analysis, and application, students examine the relationship between language, logic, and meaning
while developing skills to assess and construct effective arguments related to contemporary social
issues.
class_notes:
This class is part of the Chemistry for Health Careers learning community - some seats are reserved
for learning community students. Please contact the instructor with any questions.

subject: UNIV
title: Multiliteracy Tutor Training
description:
This course introduces students to writing center theory, pedagogy, and practice with
emphasis on developing oral, multimedia presentation skills requiring strategies for creating
arguments in forms that engage various audiences. Students analyze current research in writing
center studies while developing practical skills in written, oral, and multimodal communication
through hands-on tutoring experience in the Writing & Multiliteracy Center. Students learn to apply
theories in practice with diverse learners through culturally responsive tutoring approaches and gain
experience with both in-person and online tutoring modalities.
enrollment_requirements: Prerequisite UNIV 299: ENGL 105 (or Equivalent) and Sophomore Standing

subject: UNIV
title: Univ Life/College Success Xfr
description:
Facilitates transfer student success on the CI campus by assisting students in their
transition to CI; provides support in developing an individualized plan for personal, social, academic,
and professional success. Introduces transfer students to university life, the structure and policies of
the University. Development of strategies and skills to help ensure student success in college.
Introduction to campus academic and student resources, major and career exploration, academic
expectations and resources and skills necessary for success.
class_notes: This course is reserved for Yardi Scholars.

subject: UNIV
title: Us Travel Study Experience
description:
Hours: Two to six hours activity per week
Provides an opportunity for students to earn credit for travel and study within the United States.
Students study a topic or discipline associated with the travel destination. Students participate in
university sponsored travel that facilitates or enhances specialized study under the direction of
faculty from a campus academic program. Students are required to synthesize the results of their
course experience in a written, visual or presentation format. Three completions allowed.
class_notes: To be taken with MGT 326-02 study abroad course.

subject: UNIV
title: International Experience
description:
Faculty-led short term study abroad. Provides an opportunity for students to earn credit

description:
Students engage in an approved internship in which theories and skills learned in their
chosen major are applied in a particular work setting. Repeatable for a maximum of 6 units.
